claims.claim: Age assurance is a goal that can be implemented through more than one technology.
A requirement to implement age assurance can result in an independent app collecting identity data.
Identity documents can establish a person's age.
Collecting identity documents is not the only safe method of age assurance.
In many cases, collecting identity documents is riskier than other age-assurance options.
The proposed non-document age-assurance methods are imperfect.
Passport uploads are imperfect as an age-assurance method.
A service may need confidence that a person belongs to an age range such as under 13, 13 to 15, or adult.
Services rarely need a person's legal name, address, document number, and photograph for age assurance.
A collection of legal names, addresses, document numbers, and photographs constitutes a valuable data repository.
A breach, subpoena, or internal misuse of such a repository can expose substantially more personal information than age alone.
Document-based age assurance can exclude people who lack qualifying credentials or cannot safely present them.
